content_units: You already have a credible foundation for an operations analyst move. With   6 years in customer support leadership  , plus   QA coaching, Zendesk, SQL basics, and workflow design  , you are well-positioned for analyst roles that sit close to support, CX operations, service operations, or business operations.
- Your target of   EUR 55,000–70,000   is realistic in Amsterdam for:
- analyst roles in tech, SaaS, fintech, marketplaces, and scale-ups
- candidates who can show measurable process improvement and working-level analytics
- Strongest transition path:   customer support lead → support operations / CX operations analyst → broader operations analyst
- Fastest route: leverage your domain expertise rather than competing immediately for highly technical BI/data analyst roles
- Main unlocks: stronger   SQL, spreadsheet modeling, dashboarding, metrics storytelling, and process documentation
Option 1: Process improvement ownership   You already redesign workflows and improve team execution   Direct fit for operations analysis
Option 2: QA and coaching analytics   QA score trends, root-cause patterns, and agent performance insights are analyst-adjacent work   Strong evidence of analytical judgment
Option 3: Zendesk systems fluency   Ticket flows, macros, SLAs, tags, automation, and reporting are operational systems experience   Valuable for CX/ops analyst roles
Option 4: Cross-functional problem solving   Team leads often coordinate with product, training, workforce, and policy teams   Shows stakeholder management
Option 5: KPI management   You likely track CSAT, QA, SLA, backlog, AHT, escalation rates, and resolution quality   Core analyst language
Stop framing yourself primarily as a people manager. Frame yourself as a   data-informed operations improver  .
Customer Support Team Lead transitioning into Operations Analyst   Process Improvement, QA Analytics, Zendesk, SQL, Workflow Design

Operations-focused support leader with 6 years of experience improving service quality, agent performance, and workflow efficiency. Experienced in QA coaching, Zendesk administration/reporting, KPI tracking, root-cause analysis, and process design. Building stronger SQL, dashboarding, and operational analytics capabilities to transition into Operations Analyst roles in Amsterdam.
Rewrite your experience bullets like this
Convert task-based bullets into   problem → action → result   bullets.
- Managed a team of support agents
- Analyzed recurring ticket quality issues and redesigned QA coaching workflows, improving QA compliance by   X%
- Built weekly Zendesk reporting for SLA, backlog, and resolution trends, enabling managers to prioritize staffing and process fixes
- Reduced repeat contacts by   X%   by identifying top contact drivers and standardizing macros and escalation paths
- Mapped support workflows and removed handoff bottlenecks, cutting average resolution time by   X%
- Partnered with training/product teams to identify root causes behind   top 3 ticket drivers  , improving customer experience and operational efficiency
Keywords to add for ATS relevance
Weeks 1-2   Reposition your profile   Rewrite CV; optimize LinkedIn; collect impact metrics; identify 20 target companies in Amsterdam   Analyst-ready CV + LinkedIn
Weeks 3-4   Strengthen SQL fundamentals   SELECT, WHERE, GROUP BY, JOINs, CASE, CTE basics; practice support/ops datasets   12-15 SQL query examples
Weeks 5-6   Build spreadsheet and KPI fluency   Pivot tables, XLOOKUP, SUMIFS, cohort-style tracking, trend analysis, scenario planning   Ops metrics workbook
Weeks 7-8   Learn dashboard storytelling   Use Tableau, Power BI, or Looker Studio; create SLA/backlog/CSAT dashboard; write insights   1 polished dashboard project
Weeks 9-10   Deepen process analysis   Learn process mapping, SOP writing, root-cause methods, basic experimentation thinking   Workflow redesign case study
Weeks 11-12   Job-market packaging   Build portfolio, tailor 10 applications, practice case/interview stories, refine salary narrative   Portfolio + application pack
- Rewrite your CV for analyst roles, not support leadership alone
- Create a master achievement bank with numbers:
- Update LinkedIn headline and About section with operations/analytics keywords
- Save 30 relevant job descriptions and note repeating skills
- repeat contact analysis by issue type
Weeks 5-6: Excel or Google Sheets for ops work
- Create a weekly operations review workbook with tabs for volume, SLA, backlog, QA, CSAT, and staffing assumptions.
- “How I reduced avoidable escalations in a support workflow”
- Include current-state map, pain points, proposed redesign, expected KPI impact
- Build 2-3 portfolio pieces into clean PDFs or Notion pages
- Tailor CV for each application cluster:
- Practice analyst interview stories using STAR
- Prepare for metric and case questions:
- How would you investigate SLA decline?
- How would you prioritize process fixes?
Skill Gaps to Close and Portfolio Projects to Build
Option 1: SQL from basic to working analyst level   Need confidence with joins, aggregations, date logic, and business questions   Highest priority
Option 2: Dashboarding   Need one BI tool and executive-style KPI presentation   High hiring impact
Option 3: Structured analysis   Need clearer root-cause, process mapping, and experiment framing   Helps interviews and portfolio
Option 4: Financial/operational thinking   Learn efficiency, capacity, throughput, cost-to-serve basics   Important for broader ops roles
Portfolio projects that match your background
Option 1: Support KPI Dashboard   Build a dashboard from sample ticket data showing SLA, backlog, QA, CSAT, ticket drivers   Best first portfolio piece
Option 2: Workflow Redesign Case Study   Map a broken support process, identify bottlenecks, propose fixes, estimate KPI impact   Strong bridge from team lead to analyst
Option 3: SQL Analysis Pack   10-15 queries with short business insights on support or operations data   Shows analyst readiness
Option 4: Weekly Ops Review Pack   Spreadsheet model with trends, staffing assumptions, backlog aging, and action notes   Useful for interviews
What hiring managers want to see
- You can   find a problem in messy operations
- You can   recommend a practical fix
- You can   communicate to non-technical stakeholders
Amsterdam Job Search Strategy and Quick Actions
- “I’m moving from support leadership into operations analysis, with hands-on experience in process improvement, KPI reporting, QA analytics, and workflow design.”
- “My edge is that I understand how operational issues appear in frontline teams and how to translate them into measurable improvements.”
- international companies with English-speaking teams in Amsterdam
Application strategy for the next 9 months
- Months 4-6: apply selectively to   support ops / CX ops / service ops analyst   roles
- Months 7-9: expand to broader   operations analyst / business operations analyst   roles
